answer: A Code contribution approved in peer review backed by a refundable deposit makes identity cost real work: the code contribution is reviewed line by line, the refundable deposit is released only when the work is accepted, and a rejected submission costs the applicant time and money, so a Sybil farm must produce genuine, reviewed output for every fake account it wants. Reviewers look for the pigment that does not belong: work with no substance behind it. When the island settles over the grove, the work holds because every task carried its own review.
